name: Untouchables
label: Dischord
lede: Ian MacKaye's kid brother on vocals, a drummer who'd never played drums, a singer who kept passing out, and a song Sonic Youth covered eleven years after the band quit.

eras.title: The Teen Idles' little brothers
eras.text: Wilson High School in Northwest D.C. produced most of the city's first hardcore bands. The Untouchables were the younger crew, close friends with the Teen Idles, fronted by Alec MacKaye, Teen Idle Ian MacKaye's little brother.

years.p: [[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]], [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]]'s younger brother, born in 1965, sings. [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]] plays guitar, [[Bert Queiroz|d657171b-961c-4078-ab84-90b2c69f0095]] bass, Rich Moore drums.

years.h: The Untouchables debut in a basement with [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]]
years.p: Dischord says the Untouchables and the Teen Idles debuted together in a basement in December 1979. The scene was small enough that headliners and openers were the same circle of friends.

eras.title: Passing out, holding on
eras.text: The Untouchables played hard and mostly at home. 1980 brought their only recordings, one road trip to Norfolk, and a crisis when drummer Rich Moore left for college that nearly ended them.

years.h: Alec MacKaye gets carried out of Untouchables shows
years.p: The Untouchables' sets are wild. Dischord says Alec MacKaye had to be carried out of a number of shows after hyperventilating and passing out.

years.big: A drummer who had never played drums
q: The band decided it was curtains for them.
years.h: Drummer Rich Moore leaves, and Danny Ingram volunteers
years.p: Rich Moore leaves for college. Meeting at a Roy Rogers, the Untouchables decide they're finished, until [[Danny Ingram|41959411-d1b4-4954-af09-087ac72f69ab]] volunteers to play drums, despite never having played them.
years.xp:
Dischord's history puts the meeting at the Roy Rogers fast-food restaurant and the verdict on the table: curtains. Danny Ingram's offer kept the Untouchables going into 1981.

It also started a drumming career that ran through [[Youth Brigade|7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c]], [[Strange Boutique|0ee0668b-fa1d-4db1-ac8c-43a3ad1272c0]], [[Dot Dash|fce03e2d-8138-4418-b29e-499f61c6800e]] and, per Wikipedia, [[Swervedriver|fa6c7999-ff65-486b-9e18-bcb59d6db2f0]].

years.h: The Untouchables' only out-of-town show: Norfolk
years.p: The Untouchables mostly play D.C. Their one out-of-town show is in Norfolk, Virginia, with the Teen Idles.

eras.title: Until the plug was pulled
eras.text: The Untouchables ended the way they played: on someone else's gear at someone else's show at the 9:30 club. Within months the members were all over the next wave of D.C. bands, from Youth Brigade to Faith.

years.h: The Untouchables' last show, on somebody else's bill
years.p: At a [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]], [[SOA|e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb]] and [[Black Market Baby|5fcf3f0f-0945-4269-a6a5-9f63c385c1f4]] show at the 9:30 club, the Untouchables grab the gear and play a [[Sham 69|33235ed4-d5bd-42cd-b77c-de646c36c8c6]] song until the plug gets pulled. It's their final appearance.

years.h: Alec MacKaye is the kid on the Minor Threat EP cover
years.p: Untouchables singer Alec MacKaye is the boy on the cover of Minor Threat's first EP, an image that shows up again on Minor Threat's Complete Discography.

years.h: Untouchables members join Youth Brigade and Faith
years.p: Danny Ingram and Bert Queiroz join [[Nathan Strejcek|b53e7b75-696d-43f5-98ff-bc3d104e0d74]] in [[Youth Brigade|7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c]]. By fall 1981, Alec MacKaye is singing for [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]] with SOA veterans Michael Hampton and Ivor Hanson.

years.h: The Untouchables' Hit & Run demos land on Flex Your Head
years.p: Rat Patrol, Nic Fit and I Hate You, from the Untouchables' spring 1980 demos at the Hit & Run basement studio, open Dischord's sampler after the Teen Idles.
years.xp: The Untouchables and the Teen Idles recorded their first demos at Hit & Run in spring 1980, and the tapes got passed all over the D.C. scene before Dischord put three songs on Flex Your Head.

eras.title: Nic Fit gets a second life
eras.text: A band with four recorded songs kept turning up in places nobody expected, most loudly when Sonic Youth covered the Untouchables' Nic Fit on the major-label album Dirty.

years.p: Sonic Youth put their version of the Untouchables' Nic Fit on Dirty, their 1992 album. A minute-long basement-tape song from 1980 ends up on a DGC record.
years.xp:
By then the Untouchables were long into other lives. Eddie Janney had played in [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]], [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] and more; Bert Queiroz and Rich Moore had both played in [[The Meatmen|312c14d9-7897-4608-944a-c5b1c76ae682]] and started R&B Records together.

Alec MacKaye went on to [[Ignition|3cb2b7d6-1f0b-4ac5-b67f-52132f3d3b61]] and [[The Warmers|af0dea4e-c501-47f2-8695-129f254d425f]], and works as chief preparator at the Phillips Collection in Washington.

years.h: The Untouchables on 20 Years of Dischord
years.p: Dischord includes the Untouchables on its anniversary box set and the rare-and-unreleased collection that goes with it.

years.h: Nic Fit in the film American Hardcore
years.p: The Untouchables' Nic Fit is featured in American Hardcore, the documentary built on Steven Blush's oral history.
